notes: §1985:XIII.3.19.3 SR4: "Data-name-2 must be one of the data-names specified in the CONTROL clause for this report. Data-name-2 must not be a lower level control than the associated control for the report group in which the RESET phrase appears." and FINAL must appear in the CONTROL clause. ResolveReports sets the RESET level by ControlLevelOf (refusing a non-operand or an absent FINAL) and ScreenResetLevel refuses, below 2002, a level index greater than the footing's (COBOL6824). Probes at --std 85: RESET ON WS-B in CF WS-A (witness) and in CF FINAL refused; RESET ON WS-AMT and RESET ON FINAL without FINAL in CONTROL refused (COBOL0899, citing §2023:13.18.54.3 SR8 at 85); RESET ON WS-A in CF WS-A ran with totals 00010 and 00010, RESET ON FINAL ran with 00010 and 00020; --std 2002 refuses the same-level form. Gap: ControlLevelOf compares the WRITTEN reference (SameOperandAs), so CONTROLS ARE FINAL WS-A OF G1 WS-B with RESET ON WS-A is refused although WS-A is one of the data-names the CONTROL clause specifies (§1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR1 lets it be qualified there; data-name-2 may not be qualified, §1985:III.2). kb/Work PB5423 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read3/rd-03.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Data-name-2 must not be a lower level control than the associated control for the report group in which the RESET phrase appears."; 2023: "If the current report group is a control footing, its level of control shall be a lower level than that of data-name-3.". Both require RESET's operand or FINAL to be a CONTROL operand. 1985 also allows the footing's own control level; 2023 requires a strictly higher level and refuses equal.
